title: Meet Zscript

lessons.title: Add your first script
lessons.desc: Paste the script above into the editor and add it to a chart. Then change 20 to 5 and to 100. Write one sentence about how the line changes.
lessons.descHtml: Paste the script above into the editor and add it to a chart. Then change 20 to 5 and to 100. Write one sentence about how the line changes.

lessons.title: Rename and recolor
lessons.desc: Change the title to your own name and add color=color.orange to the plot call. Add it again.
lessons.descHtml: Change the title to your own name and add color=color.orange to the plot call. Add it again.

bodyHtml:
Zscript is the small language you use to build your own chart indicators on TradeZoro. You write a few lines, add them to the chart, and your idea is drawn on the candles. It is free for every member.

In this lesson you add your first script and learn what its four parts do.

//@zscript 1
indicator("My first line", overlay=true)
average = ta.sma(close, 20)
plot(average, title="20-bar average")

The four parts

  • Header: //@zscript 1 says this is Zscript, version 1.
  • Declaration: indicator(...) names the script. overlay=true puts it on the price chart.
  • Logic: average = ta.sma(close, 20) makes a value from the closing prices.
  • Drawing: plot(...) shows it.

Press Add to chart and a line follows price. Change 20 to 50 and add it again: the line gets smoother. Changing a number and looking is how you learn.

Education only. Not financial advice. A line on a chart describes the past; it does not promise anything.

Quick quiz

What does overlay=true do?

overlay=true draws on the price chart. Without it the script gets its own pane below.

What must be the first line of every Zscript file?

The header line tells the editor which language and version this is.

title: Bars and series

lessons.title: Two-bar change
lessons.desc: Plot close minus close[2] as a histogram. Which bars are missing at the left edge, and why?
lessons.descHtml: Plot close minus close[2] as a histogram. Which bars are missing at the left edge, and why?

lessons.title: Safe change
lessons.desc: Use nz() so the first bar shows 0 instead of nothing.
lessons.descHtml: Use nz() so the first bar shows 0 instead of nothing.

bodyHtml:
A chart is a row of bars. Zscript runs your script once for every bar, oldest to newest. On each run, close means the close of the bar being worked on.

A value that has one number per bar is a series. To see an older value, use square brackets: close[1] is the close one bar ago.

//@zscript 1
indicator("Bar change")
change1 = close - close[1]
plot(change1, "Change", style=plot.style_histogram)

On the first bar there is nothing before it, so close[1] is na: not available. Math with na gives na, and plots skip it. Use nz(x) to swap na for zero, or na(x) to test for it.

You can only look back. Zscript has no way to read a bar that has not happened yet.

Quick quiz

What is close[3]?

Square brackets look back by that many bars.

What does na mean?

na means not available. Plots skip it.

title: Values, types and colors

lessons.title: Three colors
lessons.desc: Color volume green on up bars, red on down bars, and gray when close equals open.
lessons.descHtml: Color volume green on up bars, red on down bars, and gray when close equals open.

lessons.title: Soft color
lessons.desc: Use color.new(...) to make the green 60 percent transparent.
lessons.descHtml: Use color.new(...) to make the green 60 percent transparent.

bodyHtml:
Every value has a type: int (whole numbers), float (decimals), bool (true or false), string (text) and color. Zscript usually works the type out for you.

= creates a value. := changes one that already exists. x ? a : b picks a when x is true, else b.

//@zscript 1
indicator("Up or down volume")
up = close >= open
plot(volume, "Volume", color=up ? color.green : color.red, style=plot.style_columns)

Colors: #03c988, color.red, or color.new(base, transparency) where 0 is solid and 100 invisible.

Quick quiz

Which creates a brand new value?

A single = creates. := only changes something that exists.

What does color.new(color.red, 100) look like?

Transparency 100 is fully see-through.

title: Moving averages and indicators

lessons.title: Add RSI
lessons.desc: Build an indicator in its own pane: RSI(14) with hline(30) and hline(70).
lessons.descHtml: Build an indicator in its own pane: RSI(14) with hline(30) and hline(70).

lessons.title: Bands
lessons.desc: Plot Bollinger Bands with ta.bb and shade between the outer lines using fill().
lessons.descHtml: Plot Bollinger Bands with ta.bb and shade between the outer lines using fill().

bodyHtml:
Most indicators are one function call. The ta namespace holds them: ta.sma, ta.ema, ta.rsi, ta.atr, ta.macd and many more.

//@zscript 1
indicator("Two averages", overlay=true)
fast = ta.ema(close, 9)
slow = ta.ema(close, 21)
plot(fast, color=color.green)
plot(slow, color=color.red)

Some functions give back several values. Take them apart with square brackets: [mid, up, lo] = ta.bb(close, 20, 2.0).

Call ta functions on every bar, not inside an if. They keep a running memory, and skipping bars gives wrong answers.

Quick quiz

Which is a fast, reactive average?

EMA weights recent bars more.

Where should ta functions be called?

They keep a running history that needs every bar.

title: Decisions and signals

lessons.title: Add a filter
lessons.desc: Only mark an up cross when close is also above a 100-bar SMA.
lessons.descHtml: Only mark an up cross when close is also above a 100-bar SMA.

lessons.title: Color the pane
lessons.desc: Use bgcolor to tint the background green while fast is above slow.
lessons.descHtml: Use bgcolor to tint the background green while fast is above slow.

bodyHtml:
A condition is a true or false value for each bar. ta.crossover(a, b) is true on the bar where a moves above b.

//@zscript 1
indicator("Cross marks", overlay=true)
fast = ta.ema(close, 9)
slow = ta.ema(close, 21)
plotshape(ta.crossover(fast, slow), "Up", shape.triangleup, location.belowbar, color.green)
plotshape(ta.crossunder(fast, slow), "Down", shape.triangledown, location.abovebar, color.red)

Use if / else to choose, and and, or, not to combine conditions. This lesson shows a rule on a chart. It is a teaching sample, not a trading system.

Quick quiz

When is ta.crossover(a, b) true?

A cross is an event on a single bar.

What joins two conditions so both must be true?

and needs both.

title: Remembering with var

lessons.title: Reset each day
lessons.desc: Make the counter go back to 0 at the start of every day (hint: dayofmonth != dayofmonth[1]).
lessons.descHtml: Make the counter go back to 0 at the start of every day (hint: dayofmonth != dayofmonth[1]).

lessons.title: Track the highest close
lessons.desc: Keep the highest close so far in a var float and plot it.
lessons.descHtml: Keep the highest close so far in a var float and plot it.

bodyHtml:
Normal values start fresh on every bar. A var value is set once and keeps what you give it.

//@zscript 1
indicator("Count green bars")
var int greens = 0
if close > open
    greens := greens + 1
plot(greens)

Use var for running totals, the last signal price, or a drawing you update. varip also keeps values between ticks of the newest bar; most scripts never need it.

Quick quiz

Which keyword keeps a value from bar to bar?

var is set once and then kept.

How do you change an existing value?

:= changes; = creates; == compares.

title: Inputs

lessons.title: Three inputs
lessons.desc: Add a length, a color and a show-labels switch to one of your scripts.
lessons.descHtml: Add a length, a color and a show-labels switch to one of your scripts.

lessons.title: Pick list
lessons.desc: Use input.string with options to let the user choose between SMA and EMA, then switch on it.
lessons.descHtml: Use input.string with options to let the user choose between SMA and EMA, then switch on it.

bodyHtml:
Make your script tunable with input.*. Each call adds a control to the settings dialog.

//@zscript 1
indicator("Tunable average", overlay=true)
len = input.int(20, "Length", minval=2, maxval=500)
src = input.source(close, "Source")
plot(ta.sma(src, len))

Give each input a plain title and a sensible default, set a min and max so nobody can type 0 as a length, and use group= to keep long lists tidy.

Quick quiz

Why set minval?

Limits keep the settings sensible.

Which input gives a color picker?

input.color.

title: Loops, arrays and functions

lessons.title: Write a function
lessons.desc: Write range(h, l) that returns high minus low as a percent of close, and plot it.
lessons.descHtml: Write range(h, l) that returns high minus low as a percent of close, and plot it.

lessons.title: Count in a loop
lessons.desc: Use for to count how many of the last 10 closes were above their open.
lessons.descHtml: Use for to count how many of the last 10 closes were above their open.

bodyHtml:
A for loop repeats. An array is a list. A function names a piece of logic.

//@zscript 1
indicator("Last 5 closes average")
var prices = array.new<float>()
array.push(prices, close)
if array.size(prices) > 5
    array.shift(prices)
plot(array.avg(prices))
mid(h, l) => (h + l) / 2

Loops run on every bar, so keep them short. A built-in such as ta.highest is almost always faster than the same loop. Zscript stops runaway loops with a clear error.

Quick quiz

Why keep loops short?

Cost multiplies by thousands of bars.

What does array.push do?

push appends.

title: Drawing: labels, lines, boxes and tables

lessons.title: Pivot lows
lessons.desc: Add green labels at pivot lows.
lessons.descHtml: Add green labels at pivot lows.

lessons.title: Last-bar table
lessons.desc: Show ATR and RSI in a table written only on barstate.islast.
lessons.descHtml: Show ATR and RSI in a table written only on barstate.islast.

bodyHtml:
Plots are one value per bar. Drawings are objects you create and change: label.new, line.new, box.new, table.new.

//@zscript 1
indicator("Pivots", overlay=true)
ph = ta.pivothigh(high, 5, 5)
if not na(ph)
    label.new(bar_index - 5, ph, "H", style=label.style_label_down)

A pivot needs bars on both sides to be confirmed, so it is known five bars late. Placing the label at bar_index - 5 puts it where the pivot really was, and never reads a future bar.

Each kind has a maximum on screen. The oldest are removed when you exceed it, so delete what you no longer need.

Quick quiz

Why is a pivot known late?

You cannot confirm a peak until later bars fall away.

Which is a drawing?

label.new creates a drawing object.

title: Our data: order book, order flow, GEX and options

lessons.title: Delta bars
lessons.desc: Plot flow.delta as columns, green above zero and red below.
lessons.descHtml: Plot flow.delta as columns, green above zero and red below.

lessons.title: Two kinds
lessons.desc: Plot gex.callwall and opt.range("expected") on one chart. What shows if one is missing for your plan?
lessons.descHtml: Plot gex.callwall and opt.range("expected") on one chart. What shows if one is missing for your plan?

bodyHtml:
Zscript can read the extra data TradeZoro charts show. book.* is the order book, flow.* is order flow, gex.* is GEX levels and opt.* is ZoroOptions numbers.

//@zscript 1
indicator("Delta and walls", overlay=false)
plot(flow.delta, "Delta", style=plot.style_columns)
plot(gex.callwall, "Call wall")

These follow your plan like the charts do. If your plan does not include a kind of data, the call returns na and you see one short notice. Always protect your math with nz().

Every value is the one known at that bar: no peeking ahead. GEX and options numbers are updates stored a few minutes at a time, not an instant feed.

Quick quiz

What does a data call return if your plan lacks it?

The script keeps running with na.

Can a script read future order book data?

Data is always as of the bar.

lessons.desc: Fire alert() only when barstate.isconfirmed is true.
lessons.descHtml: Fire alert() only when barstate.isconfirmed is true.

bodyHtml:
alertcondition(condition, title, message) declares a rule that shows in the chart's alert dialog.

alertcondition(ta.crossover(close, ta.sma(close, 50)), "Above 50", "Close crossed above the 50 SMA")

request.security(symbol, timeframe, expression) reads a value from another timeframe or symbol. Add [1] to use the last finished higher-timeframe bar, so the value never changes under your feet.

Quick quiz

Why add [1] after a higher-timeframe value?

The current higher-timeframe bar is still changing.

What does barstate.isconfirmed tell you?

It is true once the bar closed.

lessons.title: Describe your script
lessons.desc: Write a 3-sentence description for the script you are proudest of, with no claims about results.
lessons.descHtml: Write a 3-sentence description for the script you are proudest of, with no claims about results.

bodyHtml:
Scripts from other members run in your browser, inside a locked room with no network, no storage and no access to the page. They also have work limits: the first run must finish in 20 seconds, loops have a turn cap, and arrays and drawings have size caps.

Errors show a line and column, say what is wrong in plain English, and often suggest a fix ("Did you mean ta.sma?").

When your script is ready, Publish it to the Script Library. Choose open source (people can read it) or protected (people can use it but not read it), and free or paid. Publishing is free. Say honestly what the script does and never claim results.

Education only. Not financial advice.

Quick quiz

What is a protected script?

Protected means the source stays hidden.

Can a script open a web connection?

The sandbox has no network.
